title: A feasibility study to investigate microbreaks during minimally invasive surgery
summary:
Minimally invasive surgery has become standard practice in many areas of modern surgery due to its advantages for patients. However, performing minimally invasive surgery can cause physical discomfort for surgeons as they have to maintain static positions or awkward postures for long periods of time during such operations. Such static load can also affect surgical assistants and nurses. One way to reduce the risk factors is to take short active breaks during surgery. 
The study involves observing surgical teams as they implement microbreaks. The microbreak exercises focus on neck, back, and shoulders and are easy to perform. Our study evaluates the feasibility of microbreaks in minimally invasive surgery and is focused on the entire surgical team rather than on individuals or the precise execution of the exercises. Microbreaks are guided by an audio file and are carried out after approximately every 30 minutes for 1.5 minutes each. The surgeon decides whether a microbreak is possible at the indicated time. Questionnaires are used to collect additional data on the feasibility, practicality, and acceptability of the microbreaks at the beginning of the study, after surgery, and in the final phase of the study.

interventions.name:
The feasibility study evaluates the acceptability and practicality of microbreaks in minimally invasive surgery (n=20). 
The microbreaks were developed as active breaks in collaboration with members of a surgical team and adapted for the study.
